messages:
incident-bot: ALERT: spike in routing fallbacks detected for customer-facing inference endpoints (percent fallbacks -> eu-west increased from ~1% to 28% starting 10m ago). auto-escalation to on-call. link: https://dashboard.redwood.internal/alerts/1832504321

emily-support: @dave-oncall getting a flurry of customer tickets "responses slower / wrong model" — they say queries routed to a smaller quantized variant in eu-west and results are lower-quality :disappointed:

dave-oncall: on it. paging @sanjay (eng-oncall) and @carol-sre. will join in 2m.

sanjay: joining. initial look: routing policy migration job ran ~12m ago from infra-team. looks like a schema change removed deprecated field "fallback_region" and migration defaulted to the nearest-region fallback logic which maps to eu-west for some us zones.

maria-swe: wait — we rolled the schema change in the config-service at 1832502000. Wasn't the migration supposed to map deprecated field to "fallback": null to keep previous behavior?

lisa-eng: we added strict matching in the new schema. deprecated field removal path sets fallback to nearest-region if missing. bad default.

carol-sre: impact: live production routes for a subset of customers got their explicit fallback unset -> autoset to eu-west -> cross-region fallbacks + wrong model variants served. customers in us got higher latency and lower quality.

emily-support: I have 5 P1-ish tickets from two paying customers complaining about hallucinations and longer TTF first token. They flagged timestamps around 12:20 UTC.

dave-oncall: mitigation plan: 1) stop migration job 2) roll back config-service to previous version 3) patch routing policy defaults to explicit no-fallback for this batch 4) open customer-facing status note. who can make the rollback?

sanjay: I can rollback the config-service to 2024-11-17 build (pre-migration). will run in 2m.

opsbot: Deploy started by sanjay (build 2024-11-17-rc). CI/CD job: #deploy-4432 status: started.

lisa-eng: also patching a targeted revert for affected policy docs to re-add explicit "fallback: none" so they don't pick the new default. creating a small script to find affected tenants.

maria-swe: can we get a quick query showing which tenants saw fallback != original? I can help write the query.

sanjay: running audit query: 
```
SELECT tenant_id, route_id, original_fallback, current_fallback
FROM routing_audit
WHERE migration_batch = 'nov-17-schema' AND current_fallback != original_fallback
```
results streaming... found ~42 routes across 7 tenants.

carol-sre: rollback complete. config-service now v2024-11-17. watch the routing logs for rollback effects.

opsbot: Deploy finished by sanjay (build 2024-11-17-rc). CI/CD job: #deploy-4432 status: success.

emily-support: customers acknowledging the fix but asking for root cause. prepping replies.

lisa-eng: I pushed the patch that re-adds explicit fallback:none for the 42 routes. diff: 
```
- fallback_region: eu-west-1  # was removed by migration
+ fallback: none  # explicitly keep previous behavior
```
applied via config writer job #cfg-778.

opsbot: Config writer job #cfg-778 status: success.

carol-sre: monitoring: fallback rate back to baseline ~1.1% over last 2m. latency for affected tenants trending down. quality reports being tracked.

emily-support: updating customers: sent templated note + specific note to the two largest tenants. they asked for a postmortem and timeline.

maria-swe: initial RCA notes: schema migration removed support for deprecated field without a safe mapping; migration defaulted to nearest-region fallback. The nearest-region mapping maps some us zones to eu-west -> cross-region fallbacks and wrong model variants.

sanjay: immediate followups: 1) add validation to migration job to error if deprecated field present and no explicit new field mapping 2) add canary to config migrations (10 tenants) 3) publish a migration rollback runbook 4) add e2e test that ensures fallback mapping preserves original route semantics

lisa-eng: proposing short-term guard: add a flag in config-service to treat missing fallback as "preserve_existing_value" instead of applying nearest-region default. will open PR.

carol-sre: paging/handoff: I'm on call for next 30m then handoff to @dave-oncall for incident wrap. please ensure SLO notes updated.

emily-support: tally of customer impact: 2 enterprise tenants affected, 42 routes, approx 3.5k requests routed to wrong variant, severity: high for those tenants. we've scheduled customer follow-up calls.

dave-oncall: thanks team. immediate mitigations done. please capture timeline and blame-free notes. we'll run a formal postmortem tomorrow 15:00 UTC. owners: migration validation (sanjay), default-behavior patch (lisa-eng), customer comms (emily-support), postmortem writeup (maria-swe).

sanjay: opening an incident tracker: INC-2024-18325 with timeline and artifacts. adding logs and queries.

lisa-eng: quick snippet of the problematic migration logic for the postmortem: 
```
# before
fallback_region = cfg.pop('fallback_region', None)
# migration: if fallback_region is None -> set nearest_region()
cfg['fallback'] = fallback_region or nearest_region(cfg['region'])
```
bad default: nearest_region() picks eu-west for some us zone codes.

maria-swe: postmortem action items (short):
- validate and fail migrations that drop deprecated fields without explicit mapping (owner: sanjay)
- default behavior change: treat missing as preserve (owner: lisa-eng)
- add canary window + metric guardrails to migration runner (owner: carol-sre)
- customer remediation checklist and notification template (owner: emily-support)
- run a mock migration on staging with production snapshot (owner: maria-swe)

emily-support: leaving notes for CS to proactively reach out to customers impacted and offer remediation credits if needed.

dave-oncall: incident declared resolved for now. monitoring for 24h. please add any late evidence to INC-2024-18325. good job triaging and rolling back quickly :thumbsup:

incident-bot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status=resolved scope=partial impact=some-customers summary="routing migration defaulted fallback -> eu-west causing cross-region fallbacks and wrong model variants; rollback applied" incident_id=INC-2024-18325

carol-sre: after-action note: let's also add a config lint that warns when deprecated fields are present so the migration doesn't silently touch them.

maria-swe: agreed. I'll draft the postmortem and link to the migration PR and audit query.

emily-support: closing customer loop: called and emailed the two tenants. they appreciated the fast response and asked for the postmortem when ready.

lisa-eng: PR up: https://git.redwood/repo/config-service/pull/911 - adds preserve_existing fallback behavior behind feature flag. requesting review.

sanjay: will land migration validation tomorrow morning UTC. leaving handoff to dave for any followups.

dave-oncall: handing off to rotation tomorrow. thanks everyone.

opsbot: Reminder: create postmortem doc at https://wiki.redwood/incidents/INC-2024-18325 (owner: maria-swe)
